UNDER-CLUSTERING RULED OUT: every non-member within 40 cm is at 57-174 deg from the axis (nearest in angle is 28013 at 14.6 cm / 59.0 deg, 0.8 MeV); the acceptance plot shows NO non-member circle anywhere in the 0-30 deg band out to 75 cm. Nothing to add. STUB-TRAIL PATTERN, described not verdicted: the member list is body (0-11.6 cm: 58035, 58034, 58036, plus the 2-point stub 31016 at 11.6 cm / 22.2 deg) then a ~36 cm EMPTY gap then three more pass4_angle absorptions strung along the axis -- 41026 (47.3 cm, 19.5 deg, 7 pts, 3.2 cm), 39024 (53.2 cm, 25.6 deg, 6 pts, 3.2 cm, pdg 13) and 45030 (61.1 cm, 2.4 deg, 5 pts, 2.3 cm). Contrary to the pattern as described to me, these far stubs are NOT at larger angle than the mid-range members: 2.4-25.6 deg against 18.9-22.2 deg for the body, and the farthest one (45030 at 61 cm) is the most on-axis object in the whole member list. All four absorbed by pass4_angle; 39024 at 25.6 deg is the only member above the 25 deg pass-1 dashed line. 61 cm is 4.4 X0 for a 162 MeV shower so a late tail is not impossible, but 36 cm of nothing in between is not how a shower develops, and if these three are wrong the event is mildly over-clustered. I could not settle it; the energy at stake is small (three fragments of 2-3 cm against a 25 cm body). Verdict rests on the non-members, as in pilot 2.3.
